<div class="link-box">**Start here (Windows, nothing to install):** unzip the offline Windows package and double-click `run_dashboard.bat` in the folder `temporary-workers-dashboard`. Other systems: steps below.</div>

The package holds the dashboard's code, the processed data and the package list. All numbers come only from the two IRCC CSV files, from the IRCC dataset [Temporary Residents: TFWP and IMP Work Permit Holders – Monthly IRCC Updates](https://open.canada.ca/data/en/dataset/360024f2-17e9-4558-bfc1-3616485d65b9) (Open Government Licence – Canada); other official sources are used only for the policy-event notes and the note on permits and arrivals. The raw IRCC files are not included; the rebuild step downloads them itself.

# Run it on your own computer

**Windows, nothing to install.** The offline Windows package (`Mohsen_1B2_offline_windows.zip`, about 200 MB) adds R `r v$r_version` for Windows (folder `R-portable/`, the official CRAN build) and every R package the dashboard needs (`library/`, the versions in `renv.lock`). Unzip it (right-click > *Extract All*), open `temporary-workers-dashboard` and double-click `run_dashboard.bat`: the dashboard opens in your browser; close the black window to stop it. Nothing is installed, no internet is needed, and any R already on the computer is neither used nor changed.

**Any computer with R** (Windows, macOS or Linux; the smaller package `Mohsen_1B2.zip`):

1. Install R from <a href="https://cloud.r-project.org">cloud.r-project.org</a> (R `r v$r_min` or newer; built and tested with R `r v$r_version`).
2. Once, with internet, in R with the working folder set to `temporary-workers-dashboard` (`setwd("C:/path/to/temporary-workers-dashboard")`; `getwd()` should show it): `install.packages("renv")`, then `renv::restore()` for the exact versions. (Quicker alternative: `install.packages("shiny")`; the first `shiny::runApp()` then installs the other packages, about `r v$n_packages` in all.)
3. Start it: in a Terminal or Command Prompt `Rscript tools/run_local.R`, or in R `shiny::runApp()`, or on Windows double-click `run_dashboard.bat`.

It then runs offline from the processed data in the package (`r v$release_short`). **Live data** instead, in one line: `run_dashboard.bat live` (Command Prompt), `Rscript tools/run_local.R live`, or in R `Sys.setenv(TW_DATA_SOURCE = "live"); shiny::runApp()` (details below).

# Contents of the package (folder `temporary-workers-dashboard/`)

| Path | What it does |
|-------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| `app.R` | Main app: loads the data, builds the page (header, filters, `r v$n_tabs_word` tabs), links filters to tabs. |
| `R/data.R` | Reads the two IRCC CSV files, checks their layout, handles hidden small counts ("\-\-", counted as 0), builds the table the app uses, and loads the saved release. |
| `R/calc.R` | All calculations and wording: totals, shares, changes, rankings, headline cards, notes, chart titles, undercount flags. |
| `R/mod_*.R` (`r v$n_tab_mods_word` files) | One file per tab: `r v$tab_mods`. |
| `R/assistant.R`, `R/mod_help.R` | Help tab: an optional AI assistant (Google Gemini) that answers from the dashboard's own text and figures, with limits on question length and number. It needs a Gemini API key in `GEMINI_API_KEY`, which is **not** included; without it the Help tab says the assistant is unavailable and everything else works. |
| `R/mod_downloads.R`, `exports/`, `tools/build_exports.R` | Downloads tab and the three PDFs on it (this one, the user guide and the note on work permits for B.C.). `tools/build_exports.R` rebuilds them from the data with no AI; it needs Chrome, Python (python-docx) and LibreOffice. |
| `R/theme.R`, `www/styles.css` | Colours, chart style, source lines, policy-event notes, page style. |
| `data/baseline.rds`, `data/cache.rds` | The `r v$release_phrase`, processed; the dashboard shows the first; the second is used only in live mode if a download fails. |
| `run_dashboard.bat`, `tools/run_local.R`, `rebuild_data.bat` | Start the dashboard (add `live` for live data); rebuild the data from source (below). They install nothing. |
| `R-portable/`, `library/`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt` | Offline Windows package only: R (GPL), the R packages (open-source licences that allow redistribution) and their licence notices. |
| `renv.lock` | Exact package versions for `renv::restore()`. |
| `README.md`, `data_profile.md` | How to run and test; data profile (layout, definitions, checks against IRCC totals, assumptions). |
| `tests/` | Automated checks, run by `tests/testthat.R`: the data, every calculation, every tab with every filter, the running app in a browser, the live download, the Help assistant with a simulated AI service (no real calls), the Downloads PDFs, wording and speed. |
| `tools/` | `get_testdata.R` (IRCC files for the tests), `build_exports.R` (the Downloads PDFs), `build_windows_offline.R` (assembles `R-portable/` and `library/`), `deploy.R` (publishes to shinyapps.io; no passwords or keys stored), `windows_check.R` (one-command check). |

# Tests

To run them (needs internet, Chrome or Chromium, and the full package set from `renv::restore()`), from the project folder in a Terminal or Command Prompt: `Rscript tools/get_testdata.R`, then `Rscript tests/testthat.R`. `get_testdata.R` downloads IRCC's current files, which may be a newer release, so a few data checks may differ.

# Data: live mode and rebuilding (optional)

**Live mode** (`run_dashboard.bat live`, `Rscript tools/run_local.R live`, or `TW_DATA_SOURCE=live`): the app downloads the two IRCC files at startup and compares months over 12 months older than the release's latest month with the saved release. If more than 2% of those values differ by over 1% (and 5 permits), or a full-year Canada total by program differs by over 1%, the download is not used and the saved copy is shown with a notice. So a large real IRCC revision of older months would also keep the saved data. In live mode the PDFs on the Downloads tab may describe an older release; the tab says so.

<div class="facts">

**To rebuild the data from source** (internet needed, nothing to download by hand): double-click `rebuild_data.bat` or run `Rscript tools/build_cache_and_profile.R`. It downloads the two IRCC CSV files into `raw_profile/`, rebuilds the table with the app's own code, runs the checks in `data_profile.md` and compares the result cell by cell with the shipped release; `data/` is not changed. IRCC replaces the files with each monthly release, so a later download is a newer release and will not reproduce the `r v$release_date` numbers exactly; the script says so and lists the yearly totals side by side. Maintainers adopt a newer release with `--install`, then update `RELEASE_INFO` in `R/data.R` and run `tools/build_exports.R`.
</div>
